mix:core-G-X-96-4.description: Candidate composition of the S17 near-axis region: 0.96 mass fraction quartz glass G plus 0.04 mass fraction GeO2 additive X, fitted to the state-0 2 um reading.

A1.scope: Initial public specification of the fixture; internal structure not reported.
A1.statement: The public task describes S17 as a laboratory sample bearing external marking M7, with internal structure not specified.

A2.scope: Catalog revision 1 link list only; contents not yet read.
A2.statement: Catalog revision 1 links three documents: calibration/limits, material reference responses, and a typical M7 model description.

A3.scope: Typical M7 execution as described in doc:model-M7@1 revision 1; not verified on S17.
A3.statement: doc:model-M7@1 states that in the typical execution the outer coating is made of material P-A.

A4.scope: Service example inside the same document; exemplar only, no serial or location data.
A4.statement: doc:model-M7@1 places the described M7 in dry air in its usage example.

A5.scope: Explicit scope note of doc:model-M7@1 revision 1.
A5.statement: doc:model-M7@1 gives no part inventory, internal structure, serial number or actual conditions for S17, so its M7 claims cannot be transferred to S17 without check.

A6.scope: doc:references@1 revision 1, reference conditions 20 C; open set of standards, not a world material list.
A6.statement: doc:references@1 revision 1 reports five-channel responses (q1..q5) at 20 C for six named standards: quartz glass G, GeO2 additive X, polymer P-A, polymer P-B, water W and NaCl N.

A7.scope: Vector values as printed in doc:references@1 revision 1 at 20 C.
A7.statement: In doc:references@1 revision 1 the reported response vectors of P-A and P-B are identical: 0.1, 0.1, 0.8, 0.3, 0.2 on q1..q5.

A8.scope: Stated scope of the reference table; carries no S17 data.
A8.statement: doc:references@1 revision 1 declares itself an open set of standards rather than a list of all possible materials, and contains no S17-specific data.

A9.scope: Interpretation of the reference table; not an observation of S17.
A9.statement: Because P-A and P-B share the same reference vector, a match of S17's measured response to that vector cannot by itself identify the outer coating as P-A nor confirm the M7 claim.

A10.scope: Comparability of instrument channels with the document's reference basis; untested.
A10.statement: If the instrument's material_response yields the same five-channel basis q1..q5 at 20 C, S17 responses can be compared numerically with the reference table.

A11.scope: Single instrument reading at x = 0 mm, radius 2 um, state-0 (20 C).
A11.statement: material_response on S17 at x = 0 mm and radius 2 um in state-0 returns q1..q5 values 0.88, 0.224, 0.108, 0.06, 0.052.

A12.scope: Numerical similarity of one reading to a catalog standard; not a composition measurement and not proof of material.
A12.statement: The 2 um-radius S17 vector lies close to the quartz glass G reference 0.9, 0.2, 0.1, 0.05, 0.05 and far from the P-A/P-B vector, so the near-axis region behaves glass-like rather than P-A-like.

A13.scope: Instrument axis labels compared with the reference table labels.
A13.statement: The instrument reports its material_response on the same five channels q1..q5 as doc:references@1, making numerical comparison with that table legitimate for this reading.

A14.scope: Single instrument reading at x = 0 mm, radius 90 um, state-0 (20 C).
A14.statement: material_response on S17 at x = 0 mm and radius 90 um in state-0 returns q1..q5 values 0.1, 0.1, 0.8, 0.3, 0.2.

A15.scope: Numerical equality of one reading with the P-A/P-B reference vector; degeneracy prevents unique naming.
A15.statement: The 90 um-radius S17 vector equals the P-A and P-B reference vector 0.1, 0.1, 0.8, 0.3, 0.2, so the outer region is P-A-like or P-B-like and consistent with, but not proof of, the M7 P-A coating claim.

A16.scope: Interpretation of two radial probes at x = 0 mm in state-0; no interface directly observed.
A16.statement: The contrast between a glass-like 2 um core reading and a P-A/P-B-like 90 um coating reading supports a layered build with a glass-like inner region and a polymer-like outer coating.

A17.scope: Single pulse_trace on S17 in state-0 at 20 C; one instrument, one revision, no repeats.
A17.statement: pulse_trace on S17 in state-0 injected pulses at input times 0, 100, 200 ns and recorded output times 5.0, 105.0, 205.0 ns, i.e. a uniform 5 ns transit delay per pulse with no further echoes in the recorded window.

A18.scope: Interfaces named by the instrument response only; no geometric location given.
A18.statement: The pulse_trace response addresses S17 through two named interfaces, input port S17:in and output port S17:out.

A19.scope: Interpretation of one uniform-delay trace; instrument time resolution not yet known.
A19.statement: A single uniform 5 ns delay with no resolvable reflection is compatible either with a homogeneous optical path or with a layered build whose layer thicknesses are below the instrument's time resolution, so this trace does not by itself confirm the glass-core plus polymer-coating model.

A20.scope: doc:calibration@1 revision 1, stated limits of the training fixture instrument only.
A20.statement: doc:calibration@1 revision 1 states a per-channel absolute tolerance of 0.001 for material_response, that in this training fixture a mixture response equals the mass-fraction-weighted sum of component responses, that the reference library is not complete, and that a response match establishes neither unique composition nor the spatial distribution of an additive inside the measured spot.

A21.scope: doc:calibration@1 revision 1 description of the pulse_trace channel.
A21.statement: doc:calibration@1 revision 1 gives pulse_trace a time resolution of 0.001 ns on a shared clock and states that only input and output times are recorded, so the pulse path inside the sample is not observed.

A22.statement: doc:calibration@1 revision 1 gives radial_profile a contrast repeatability of 1 unit and a resolvable step of 5 units, with a boundary localizable only between adjacent sample points.

A23.scope: Fit under the fixture's additive mixing rule at 20 C, state-0; a hypothesis, and the rule is a fixture condition, not a physical law.
A23.statement: The state-0 reading at x = 0 mm, radius 2 um (0.88, 0.224, 0.108, 0.06, 0.052) is reproduced within 0.001 on all five channels by a mixture of 0.96 mass fraction quartz glass G and 0.04 mass fraction GeO2 X, so the near-axis region is glass-rich with a small additive fraction rather than pure G.

A24.scope: Reinterpretation of the single state-0 pulse_trace in light of the instrument limit; no internal path is observed.
A24.statement: Because the pulse_trace channel records only input and output times, the single uniform 5 ns delay carries no information about the number, position or thickness of internal layers, so it neither confirms nor excludes the glass-core plus polymer-coating model regardless of the 0.001 ns resolution.

A25.scope: Single non-destructive radial_profile at one section x = 0 mm, state-0 (20 C); axial symmetry not measured.
A25.statement: radial_profile on S17 at x = 0 mm in state-0 returns contrast_units 100 at r = 0, 2, 3.9 um; 160 at r = 4.1, 20, 62.4 um; 230 at r = 62.6, 90, 124.9 um; and 20 at r = 125.1 and 150 um.

A26.scope: Step sizes compared with the 5-unit resolvable step of doc:calibration@1; boundaries localized only between adjacent sample points.
A26.statement: The three contrast steps of about 60, 70 and 210 units all exceed the 5-unit resolvable step, so three radial boundaries are resolved at approximately 4.0, 62.5 and 125.0 um radius, each localized only between adjacent sample points.

A27.scope: Interpretation of one radial profile plus two material_response points at x = 0 mm in state-0; no interface directly imaged.
A27.statement: The profile supports a concentric build of at least three regions: a glass-like core out to about 4 um (contrast 100, matching the glass-like 2 um reading), a middle band 4 to 62.5 um (contrast 160), and an outer coating 62.5 to 125 um (contrast 230, containing the 90 um reading that matches the P-A/P-B vector), with contrast falling to 20 beyond 125 um toward the surroundings.

A28.scope: Radial extent inferred from the 62.5 and 125.0 um boundaries; P-A versus P-B remains degenerate.
A28.statement: The outer coating band spans roughly 62.5 to 125 um radius (thickness about 62.5 um) and its material_response matches the shared P-A/P-B vector, so the M7 outer-coating material claim is spatially consistent with this band while the composition stays ambiguous between P-A and P-B.

A29.scope: Contrast 160 band has no per-channel material_response reading yet; no match is claimed.
A29.statement: The 4 to 62.5 um band at contrast 160 is the thickest region in the profile yet matches no listed single standard by any measured response, so its material identity remains unresolved.

A30.scope: material:P-A resource revision 1; explicitly the same reference record as D02, not a new chemical analysis of S17.
A30.statement: The material:P-A resource restates the 20 C reference vector of polymer P-A as 0.1, 0.1, 0.8, 0.3, 0.2 on q1..q5, identical to doc:references@1 revision 1, and supplies no new data.

A31.scope: Interpretation of a repeated reference record; no S17-specific discriminating measurement exists yet.
A31.statement: Because the material:P-A resource only repeats the reference table, the 90 um outer-region match remains numerically degenerate between P-A and P-B and cannot yet be attributed to P-A alone.

A32.scope: Single instrument reading at x = 0 mm, radius 20 um, state-0 (20 C); one point inside the 4-62.5 um band.
A32.statement: material_response on S17 at x = 0 mm and radius 20 um in state-0 returns q1..q5 values 0.9, 0.2, 0.1, 0.05, 0.05.

A33.scope: One reading at 20 um compared with the doc:references@1 table under the 0.001 per-channel tolerance; within-spot distribution still unresolved.
A33.statement: The 20 um vector equals the quartz glass G reference 0.9, 0.2, 0.1, 0.05, 0.05 with zero deviation on all five channels, so the 160-unit middle band is glass-like rather than P-A/P-B-like and the coating band is therefore not the middle band.

A34.scope: Cross-comparison of one material_response pair with one radial_profile step at x = 0 mm, state-0; mechanism of contrast not measured.
A34.statement: The 100-unit core (0.96 G + 0.04 X, q1 = 0.88) and the 160-unit middle band (pure G, q1 = 0.90) differ by a 60-unit contrast step that is far above the 5-unit resolvable step, while their material_response differs by only about 0.02 on q1, so radial contrast and material_response are not redundant probes and the contrast difference is not explained by the five-channel response alone.

A35.scope: Single radial profile at one section; the compositional and structural cause of contrast_units is not stated by any read document.
A35.statement: No available document states what radial_profile contrast_units measure, so a 60-unit step between a nearly identical-response core and middle band cannot yet be attributed to additive content, density or another property.

A36.scope: material:additive resource revision 1; explicitly the same record as D02, not a new chemical analysis of S17.
A36.statement: The material:additive resource restates the 20 C GeO2 X reference vector 0.4, 0.8, 0.3, 0.3, 0.1 on q1..q5, identical to doc:references@1 revision 1, and supplies no additional data.

A37.scope: Fit under the fixture's mass-fraction mixing rule at 20 C, state-0; the rule is a fixture condition and additive distribution inside a spot is not resolvable per doc:calibration@1.
A37.statement: Because the 2 um probe needs an X fraction near 0.04 while the 20 um probe matches pure quartz glass G with zero deviation, the additive is most plausibly confined near the axis inside roughly the 4 um core, consistent with the 100-unit core versus 160-unit middle-band step.

A38.scope: Contract-level record of two rejected tool calls; graph unchanged, no measurements returned.
A38.statement: The attempted radial_profile at x = 500 mm and the attempted read of material:P-B were both rejected as protocol errors with no data returned, so axial uniformity and the P-A versus P-B discrimination remain untested and both rejections are access/scheduling limits rather than physical results.

QROOT.text: Исследуйте устройство образца S17 и его окружение. Сохраняйте найденные объекты, связи, основания и открытые вопросы. Различайте наблюдения, сообщения источников и гипотезы. Порядок, число объектов и глубина разбиения не заданы.

QDOC1.text: What internal structure and part inventory does doc:model-M7@1 attribute to the M7 model, and does it apply to S17?

QPA1.text: What does doc:references@1 report about material P-A, and can those reported responses be matched against S17's outer coating?

QOBS1.text: What does an optical pulse_trace on S17 at state-0 reveal about internal layers or interfaces along the sample?

QPA2.text: What response vector does S17 give under material_response at 20 C in state-0, at which radius, and which reference standard (if any) does it resemble?

QCHAN1.text: Are the instrument's material_response axes the same q1..q5 channels as the reference table, i.e. is a direct numerical comparison legitimate?

QPA3.text: What does S17 give under material_response at larger radii (20 um and 90 um) in state-0, and does the outer-coating region match P-A, P-B or another standard?

QSTRUCT1.text: Does S17 have a layered internal structure with a glass-like core and a distinct outer coating, as a pulse_trace or radial_profile could show?

QSTRUCT2.text: At what radius does the glass-like inner region give way to the P-A/P-B-like outer coating along x = 0 mm, and how thick is each region?

QRES1.text: What time resolution and minimum detectable interface spacing does the pulse clock have, and can a single uniform 5 ns delay exclude or permit internal layers in S17?

QMIX1.text: Is the near-axis region a glass G plus GeO2 X mixture near 0.96/0.04 mass fractions, and is the outer region exactly P-A/P-B within the 0.001 tolerance?

QPROF1.text: Can a radial_profile at x = 0 mm and x = 500 mm localize the core-to-coating boundary in S17 given a resolvable step of 5 units, and what boundary radius results?

QMID1.text: Which material or mixture gives the 160-unit contrast_units middle band at 4 to 62.5 um, and does a material_response at radius 20 um match any listed standard or a fitted mixture?

QAX1.text: Do radial profiles at other axial positions such as x = 500 mm reproduce the same three boundaries near 4, 62.5 and 125 um, i.e. is the layered build uniform along the axis?

QCONTRAST1.text: Why do the additive-bearing core (contrast 100) and the pure-glass middle band (contrast 160) differ by about 60 contrast units when their material_response differs by only about 0.02, and what does radial_profile contrast_units actually respond to?

QENV1.text: Is the contrast-20 region beyond about 125 um radius the surrounding medium of S17 rather than part of the sample, and can any resource name that medium for the measured condition?

QTEMP1.text: What does the available pulse_trace channel report for S17 in the 40 C state (state-1), and does the transit delay or any other recorded timing differ from the 20 C state-0 trace?

QPB1.text: Does the material:P-B resource contain anything beyond the D02 reference vector that discriminates P-B from P-A, and would that change the interpretation of S17's outer-region match?

QLOC1.text: Is the near-axis additive X confined within roughly the 4 um core radius, given that the 20 um reading inside the 4 to 62.5 um band matches pure quartz glass G with zero deviation?

QU1.reason: Catalog contents enumerated; document contents still unread, so the question stays open.

QU2.reason: The M7 document supplies only outer-coating material and an example environment, with no part inventory and no S17-specific data, so its applicability to S17 remains unresolved.

QU3.reason: The P-A reference vector is now known, but S17's coating has not been measured and P-A/P-B degeneracy prevents unique matching, so the second half of the question stays open.

QU4.reason: No pulse_trace has been run yet in state-0.

QU5.reason: The instrument returned the same five channel labels q1..q5 as the reference table, so direct numerical comparison is legitimate.

QU6.reason: Only one radius (2 um) has been probed; the outer coating region and the match question remain untested.

QU7.reason: The document supplies no part inventory and the 2 um probe fits glass, so the layer inventory and M7 applicability to S17 are still unresolved.

QU8.reason: The 90 um probe now matches the P-A/P-B vector, but the 20 um probe and the P-A versus P-B degeneracy remain unresolved.

QU9.reason: Two radial points now bracket a glass-like core and polymer-like outer region, yet no interface has been directly observed.

QU10.reason: A pulse_trace now exists and shows a single uniform 5 ns delay, but no distinct internal echoes above the recorded resolution, so the interface question stays open.

QU11.reason: The trace is consistent with both a homogeneous path and sub-resolution layers, so a layered build is neither confirmed nor excluded.

QU12.reason: doc:model-M7@1 still supplies no part inventory, and the new timing trace adds no document-level M7 structure, so S17 applicability remains unresolved.

QU13.reason: No radial interface position is resolved by two point probes or by one uniform-delay trace.

QU14.reason: doc:calibration@1 specifies 0.001 ns resolution but also states that only input and output are recorded, so no pulse_trace can observe internal interfaces in S17 at all.

QU15.reason: The 2 um reading matches no single listed standard within the 0.001 tolerance, so the resemblance question is now a mixture question and stays open.

QU16.reason: The timing method is now known to be blind to internal interfaces, so a layered build must be tested by radial profile rather than pulse_trace.

QU17.reason: The 90 um vector equals the P-A and P-B references within 0.001, but the two standards remain numerically degenerate and the 20 um probe is still unmeasured.

QU18.reason: The x = 0 mm profile resolves three boundaries at about 4.0, 62.5 and 125.0 um, all steps far above the 5-unit resolvable step.

QU19.reason: The glass-like core ends near 4 um and is followed by a 4-62.5 um band before the P-A/P-B-like 62.5-125 um coating, so the inner-to-outer transition is not a single boundary.

QU20.reason: The 160-unit middle band and the P-A/P-B degeneracy still leave the mixture decomposition unresolved.

QU21.reason: doc:model-M7@1 still supplies no part inventory or internal structure, and the next read targets a material resource to test the coating claim.

QU22.reason: The material resource returned the same P-A vector as doc:references@1 and no additional discriminating data, so the P-A versus P-B question remains open.

QU23.reason: No material_response has been taken inside the 4 to 62.5 um contrast-160 band; the 20 um probe is still pending.

QU24.reason: The 20 um probe reproduces the quartz glass G reference on all five channels within the 0.001 tolerance, so the 160-unit middle band is glass-like rather than an unlisted standard or a fitted mixture.

QU25.reason: The 20 um probe is now measured and is glass-like, so among the three planned radii only the 90 um coating remains matched to the degenerate P-A/P-B vector.

QU26.reason: The core still fits 0.96 G + 0.04 X while the 20 um band fits pure G, so the additive-bearing core versus pure-glass middle band distinction remains a hypothesis.

QU29.reason: The x = 500 mm radial_profile call was rejected with no data, so axial uniformity of the three boundaries is still untested.

QU30.reason: The material:P-B read attempt returned no data, so the P-A versus P-B degeneracy is unchanged and the coating attribution stays unresolved.

QU31.reason: No read document supplies an M7 part inventory or internal structure, so only further instrument states or material resources can bear on the M7 layered-build claim for S17.
